name: Cute number
description: Ran is especially skilled in computation and mathematics. It is said that she can do unimaginable calculation work in an instant. — Perfect Memento in Strict Sense Ran Yakumo is a cute girl who loves creating cute Maths problems. Let $$$f(x)$$$ be the minimal square number strictly greater than $$$x$$$, and $$$g(x)$$$ be the maximal square number less than or equal to $$$x$$$. For example, $$$f(1)=f(2)=g(4)=g(8)=4$$$. A positive integer $$$x$$$ is cute if $$$x-g(x) \lt f(x)-x$$$. For example, $$$1,5,11$$$ are cute integers, while $$$3,8,15$$$ are not. Ran gives you an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$. She wants you to find the smallest non-negative integer $$$k$$$ such that $$$a_i + k$$$ is a cute number for any element of $$$a$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 10^6$$$) — the length of $$$a$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ intergers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \ldots \leq a_n \leq 2\cdot 10^6$$$) — the array $$$a$$$.
output_specification: Print a single interger $$$k$$$ — the answer.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1687D — Cute number [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
